originalText:
Everyone is using Fable 5 to build funny little demos so I decided to build something better. 

Vibe coded a 3D keyboard ecom platform in @threejs and @greensock. Every key. Every switch. Every color. Customizable in real time in 3D. 

It's really amusing that whole keyboard is built at runtime using Procedural geometry. 

To achieve that kind of realistic lighting on keyboard, it used a studio environment (gradient sky + softbox panels) rendered into a PMREM cubemap for realistic reflections. Opus helped a bit more here (as Fable was failing in loop in Claude chat)

There is also custom GLSL shaders for RGB underflow/skirt and as well sRGB output encoding + explicit convertSRGBToLinear() on every material color so caps render at their exact swatch value.

I don't know any of these techniques and concepts but I have had been reading how both Fable and Opus were trying to approach this by digging into their "thinking" phase. 

Go try it, there is a cool Claude theme keyboard you would want to purchase too :D

Live: https://t.co/YaenuyXvaV
Code: https://t.co/alYsHFguYt

originalText:
I’ve been seeing a lot of slop games made with Claude Fable 5, so I wanted to build something I’d actually enjoy playing.

What better way to celebrate all the new robotics companies shipping this year than a first-person robot simulator where you clean and organize a house?

This was mostly vibe prompted into a small robotics sandbox, but it gave me a whole new appreciation for how difficult robotics actually is. Even in a game, controlling two independent arms in 3D space, lining up grasps, avoiding collisions, and making sure your own body doesn’t knock things over is surprisingly challenging 😆, It looks simple until you play.

Definitely one of the most fun projects I’ve made so far, and I want to keep expanding it. Still on the slop indie stage but the majority people watching this video will quickly forget how creating anything like this was genuinely impossible year ago and I implore you to try to one shot something like this with the models available a year ago.

originalText:
CLAUDE FABLE 5 UPDATE WILL REPLACE MANUAL TRADERS

New update will change everything for devs.

My current bot i made with Claude is still running.

+5,474.62 PnL in a few days.
(started with $100 publicly) 

And it never predicted a single candle to get there.

One dead simple rule: YES + NO < $1.

On a BTC Up/Down market, YES and NO must add up to exactly $1 at resolution.

One side ends at a dollar. 
The other ends at zero.

But the orderbook is messy and both sides trade like strangers.

So for a few seconds YES sits at 47 cents while NO sits at 49.

That's 96 cents to own BOTH sides of a market that pays a guaranteed dollar.

4 cents locked, and it does not care where Bitcoin goes.

The whole game is speed. 

Gaps close in seconds, fees eat the thin ones, and you need both legs filled before it's gone.

Here's where a better model actually changes things for us builders:

It writes tighter execution code.

Meaning less lag between spotting the gap and firing both legs. 

It also catches edge cases a dumber model misses (phantom fills, partial legs, the stuff that turns free money into a loss ).

And it backtests and debugs way faster.

Better model will open the next door for evey arb bot developer.

The gap between button-clickers and builders was already wide.

I guess tomorrow it turns into a smth different.

Check my last articles if you're into arb.

Made them free so our community of builders grow.

Peace.
